status_summary: On 2025-05-30 DOE announced termination of 24 Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations awards worth over $3.7 billion, which it said primarily funded carbon capture and sequestration and decarbonization projects. On 2025-11-14 DOE's Office of Fossil Energy announced two funding opportunities totaling up to $355 million, including a Mines and Metals Capacity Expansion opportunity with a focus area on producing critical materials from coal-based feedstocks. On 2026-07-01 DOE announced selection of five pilot projects for $75 million to recover critical minerals from coal and coal-based feedstocks, managed by NETL, while the status of DOE's continuing carbon capture research was not established.

timeline.event: The Secretary of Energy announced termination of 24 Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations awards totaling over $3.7 billion, described as primarily carbon capture and sequestration and decarbonization projects, after a case-by-case financial review.

DOE's Office of Fossil Energy announced two funding opportunities totaling up to $355 million, including up to $275 million for pilot-scale recovery of critical materials from industrial sites with a coal-based feedstocks focus area; applications were due 2025-12-15.

DOE's Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation announced $75 million for five selected pilot-scale projects (University of North Dakota, Valor Metals, CONSOL Innovations, American Resources Corporation and Peabody Energy) to recover critical minerals from coal and coal-based feedstocks, managed by NETL; selections are subject to negotiation.

title: End DOE carbon capture programs and pursue critical minerals from coal waste
uncertainties: The terminated awards were described as primarily carbon capture and decarbonization; the number that were carbon capture projects was not given. DOE's FY2026 request, Public Law 119-21 treatment of the 45Q credit, and any continuing NETL carbon capture research were not checked. Checked 2026-10-30: the FY2027 Budget appendix on govinfo.gov proposes cancelling $15.2 billion of Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act funding described in part as for carbon dioxide removal and ends ARPA-E funding for direct air capture, and adds $394 million for domestic critical minerals work; it is a request, not an enacted appropriation, and the passages read do not state what happens to NETL carbon capture research. A Mintz summary of the request (2026-04-14) says Fossil Energy and Carbon Management was renamed the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office and parts of Fossil Energy were absorbed into the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, which accounts for the office name on the 2026 awards. Overlaps c12-01 on the fossil and demonstration offices; this record is limited to the two page 376 and 377 items.
